actions.query: longitudinal studies on AI-driven training recommendation reliance and athlete self-regulation
actions.reason: Current findings are based on cross-sectional data; longitudinal research is required to determine the causal trajectory of AI dependence on athlete autonomy.

review.alternative: Athletes may intentionally outsource signals to optimize performance using superior data inputs.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing no correlation or inverse correlation between AI reliance and self-regulation metrics.

claims.statement: AI training recommendation dependence is positively associated with body signal outsourcing.

support.explanation: Statistical association established in a cohort of 381 athletes.
support.passage: AI training recommendation dependence was significantly and positively associated with body signal outsourcing tendency

review.alternative: Reduced self-regulation may be a precursor, rather than a consequence, of outsourcing body signals to AI.
review.would_change_mind: Longitudinal data showing that self-regulation increases or remains stable despite high AI dependence.

claims.statement: Body signal outsourcing in athletes is linked to a reduced sense of self-regulation.

support.explanation: This finding connects external AI reliance to a decrease in internal self-regulation capabilities.
support.passage: body signal outsourcing tendency, which was, in turn, positively associated with a reduced sense of self-regulation.

actions.limitations: Findings are based on cross-sectional questionnaire data; causal directions cannot be fully established. Long-term impacts remain unobserved.
